newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says set-aside rate to keep grain mkt balanced.
newsitem.headline: EU says set-aside rate to keep grain mkt balanced.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it proposed an unchanged 1998 cereals set-aside rate of five percent in order to keep the market balanced.

"With the aim of safeguarding against climatic problems affecting cereals and other major crops, it's necessary to maintain production potential without...rebuilding excessive public stocks," it said in a statement.
Agriculture spokesman Gerard Kiely added preliminary estimates from various organisations pointed to a slightly lower cereals crop of between 197 to 200 million tonnes in 1997.
On Friday, Coceral, the EU grain trade lobby, forecast an EU grain crop of 197.29 million tonnes in 1997/98, against 201.54 million last season.
Consumption could perhaps increase further in 1997/98 following a substantial rise last season, Kiely said, adding that cereals prices were expected to be lower.
Export prospects were also seen to be bullish, following shipments of nearly 27 million tonnes in 1996/97.
"The outlook for cereals exports is fairly positive," Kiely said.
The spokesman estimated that five percent compulsory set-aside would result in two million hectares being taken out of production in 1998.
In addition a further 2.5 million hectares is expected to be idled under a voluntary set-aside scheme.
In line with EU farm ministers' demands last month, the Commission proposed to suspend so-called penalty set-aside, for exceeding area limits, for another year to June 30, 1998.
It also proposed to ease penalties for exceeding cereals planting limits on irrigated land.
